questions.stem: A 24-year-old woman has had painful red lumps on the front of both lower legs for 5 days. Three weeks ago she had a sore throat with fever that went away without treatment. Exam shows several warm, tender, poorly defined red nodules, 2 to 4 cm wide, on both shins. None of them is ulcerated. Lab results: antistreptolysin O titer 800 IU/mL (reference below 200), ESR 46 mm/h, and a normal chest x-ray with no hilar lymph node enlargement. A deep skin biopsy of one nodule is done. Which finding is most likely?
choices: Lobular panniculitis with vasculitis of medium-sized vessels in the fat
Fibrinoid necrosis of small dermal venules with neutrophil nuclear dust (leukocytoclasis)
Noncaseating granulomas throughout the reticular dermis
Necrotic fat lobules with calcium soap deposits
Inflammation of the fibrous septa between fat lobules without vasculitis
questions.explanation: Tender, non-ulcerated nodules on both shins weeks after a streptococcal throat infection (high **antistreptolysin O**) are **erythema nodosum**, a reactive inflammation of the subcutaneous fat. Biopsy shows a **septal panniculitis**: the fibrous septa between fat lobules are thick and inflamed, and there is **no vasculitis**, so the nodules heal without ulcers or scars. The most tempting choice, lobular panniculitis with vasculitis, describes **erythema induratum** (nodular vasculitis), which favors the calves and often ulcerates.
questions.explanation_pt: Nódulos dolorosos e não ulcerados nas duas regiões pré-tibiais semanas após uma faringite estreptocócica (**antiestreptolisina O** elevada) indicam **eritema nodoso**, uma inflamação reativa do tecido adiposo subcutâneo. A biópsia mostra **paniculite septal**: os septos fibrosos entre os lóbulos de gordura ficam espessos e inflamados, e **não há vasculite**, por isso os nódulos regridem sem úlceras nem cicatrizes. A alternativa mais tentadora, paniculite lobular com vasculite, descreve o **eritema endurado** (vasculite nodular), que prefere as panturrilhas e muitas vezes ulcera.

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man started allopurinol 3 weeks ago for recurrent gout. Two days ago he developed fever and burning eyes, and today his skin is painful. Temperature is 38.9°C (102°F). There are dusky red macules with dark centers on his trunk that are merging, with flaccid blisters. His lips are crusted and bleeding, and the mouth and conjunctivae have erosions. Gentle pressure makes the epidermis peel away in sheets. A biopsy shows necrosis of the full thickness of the epidermis with only a sparse dermal infiltrate. Direct immunofluorescence is negative. Which mechanism best explains the skin damage?
choices: IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 causing loss of cell adhesion
Drug-specific CD8+ T cells triggering widespread keratinocyte apoptosis
A staphylococcal exotoxin cleaving desmoglein 1 in the upper granular layer
Drug-specific IgE crosslinked on the surface of dermal mast cells
Immune complexes depositing in the walls of small dermal venules
questions.explanation: A new high-risk drug, fever, painful dusky skin, mucosal erosions and **full-thickness epidermal necrosis** with negative immunofluorescence mean **SJS/TEN**. Drug-specific **cytotoxic CD8+ T cells** (and NK cells) release **granulysin** and use the **Fas-Fas ligand** pathway, so keratinocytes die by apoptosis across the whole epidermis. Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome also gives a positive Nikolsky sign, but its toxin splits only the upper epidermis (granular layer), spares the mucosae and mainly affects young children, so the biopsy would not show full-thickness necrosis.
questions.explanation_pt: Um fármaco novo de alto risco, febre, pele dolorosa e violácea, erosões de mucosas e **necrose epidérmica de espessura total** com imunofluorescência negativa indicam **SSJ/NET**. **Linfócitos T CD8+ citotóxicos** (e células NK) específicos para o fármaco liberam **granulisina** e usam a via **Fas-ligante de Fas**, e os queratinócitos morrem por apoptose em toda a epiderme. A síndrome da pele escaldada estafilocócica também tem sinal de Nikolsky positivo, mas sua toxina separa apenas a epiderme superior (camada granulosa), poupa as mucosas e acomete sobretudo crianças pequenas, por isso a biópsia não mostraria necrose de espessura total.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old man has had well-defined, red, scaly plaques on his lower back, behind his ears and around his umbilicus for 4 years. His father has a similar rash. The plaques worsen in winter and during stressful periods. A biopsy shows a thick epidermis with long, regular rete ridges, retained nuclei in the stratum corneum and small neutrophil collections under the surface. Which immune process most directly drives the rapid keratinocyte proliferation in his lesions?
choices: IL-23 from dendritic cells sustaining Th17 cells that secrete IL-17
IL-4 and IL-13 from Th2 cells that weaken the epidermal barrier and raise IgE
IgG autoantibodies binding to desmosomes between keratinocytes
IL-10 and TGF-beta from regulatory T cells in the upper dermis
Histamine released from IgE-coated mast cells in the dermis
questions.explanation: Chronic well-defined scaly plaques with a family history, regular epidermal thickening, **parakeratosis** and **Munro microabscesses** mean **plaque psoriasis**. Dermal dendritic cells release **IL-23**, which keeps **Th17 cells** active; their **IL-17** (with IL-22 and TNF-alpha) makes keratinocytes divide quickly and attract neutrophils, which is why IL-23 and IL-17 blockers work. The Th2 pathway (IL-4 and IL-13) drives **atopic dermatitis**, which gives itchy, poorly defined eczema with spongiosis, not sharp plaques with parakeratosis.
questions.explanation_pt: Placas descamativas crônicas e bem delimitadas, história familiar, espessamento regular da epiderme, **paraceratose** e **microabscessos de Munro** indicam **psoríase em placas**. Células dendríticas da derme liberam **IL-23**, que mantém ativos os **linfócitos Th17**; a **IL-17** produzida por eles (com IL-22 e TNF-alfa) faz os queratinócitos se dividirem rapidamente e atrai neutrófilos, por isso os bloqueadores de IL-23 e IL-17 funcionam. A via Th2 (IL-4 e IL-13) causa a **dermatite atópica**, com eczema pruriginoso mal delimitado e espongiose, e não placas nítidas com paraceratose.

questions.stem: A 4-year-old boy has had atopic dermatitis since infancy. For 2 days he has had fever and a painful rash on his face and neck, in the same areas where his eczema is worst. Temperature is 39.0°C (102.2°F). Exam shows clusters of small, uniform, punched-out erosions, many with dark red crusts; a few intact vesicles remain at the edges. His mother had a blister on her lip last week. A smear from the base of a fresh vesicle shows multinucleated giant cells. Which organism is the most likely cause?
choices: Staphylococcus aureus
Streptococcus pyogenes
Molluscum contagiosum virus
Herpes simplex virus
Coxsackievirus A6
questions.explanation: Fever with clusters of monomorphic, **punched-out erosions** spreading through areas of eczema, after contact with a cold sore, and **multinucleated giant cells** on a Tzanck smear mean **eczema herpeticum** (*Kaposi varicelliform eruption*), a widespread **HSV-1** infection of skin with a damaged barrier. It needs prompt antiviral treatment. *S. aureus* often colonizes eczema and causes impetigo with honey-colored crusts, but it does not produce multinucleated giant cells.
questions.explanation_pt: Febre com agrupamentos de **erosões monomórficas em saca-bocado** espalhando-se pelas áreas de eczema, após contato com um herpes labial, e **células gigantes multinucleadas** no esfregaço de Tzanck indicam **eczema herpético** (*erupção variceliforme de Kaposi*), uma infecção extensa pelo **HSV-1** na pele com barreira lesada. Exige tratamento antiviral imediato. O *S. aureus* coloniza com frequência o eczema e causa impetigo com crostas melicéricas, mas não produz células gigantes multinucleadas.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has had very itchy bumps on the inner wrists and ankles for 3 months. Exam shows shiny, violet, flat-topped papules with angled borders and fine white lines on their surface. The inside of both cheeks has a lacy, white, net-like pattern. Lab results: ALT 92 U/L (reference 7-40), AST 74 U/L (reference 10-40), total bilirubin 0.9 mg/dL, albumin 4.0 g/dL and platelet count 210,000/mm3. Which additional test result is most likely?
choices: IgA antibodies against tissue transglutaminase
IgG antibodies against desmoglein 3
Antibodies against hepatitis C virus
Antibodies against double-stranded DNA
Antibodies against proteinase 3 (c-ANCA)
questions.explanation: Itchy, violet, polygonal, flat-topped papules with **Wickham striae** on the wrists, plus lacy white **oral lesions**, mean **lichen planus**. Her raised aminotransferases point to chronic liver injury, and lichen planus, especially the oral form, is linked to **chronic hepatitis C** infection. Desmoglein 3 antibodies cause pemphigus vulgaris, whose oral lesions are painful raw erosions, not a lacy white network.
questions.explanation_pt: Pápulas pruriginosas, violáceas, poligonais e planas com **estrias de Wickham** nos punhos, além de **lesões orais** brancas rendilhadas, indicam **líquen plano**. As aminotransferases elevadas apontam para lesão hepática crônica, e o líquen plano, sobretudo a forma oral, está associado à infecção crônica pelo **vírus da hepatite C**. Anticorpos contra a desmogleína 3 causam pênfigo vulgar, cujas lesões orais são erosões dolorosas em carne viva, e não uma rede branca rendilhada.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy has had spots on his forehead, nose and cheeks for 1 year. Exam shows many small blackheads and skin-colored closed bumps, along with some red papules and a few pustules. His skin is oily. He has no facial flushing or visible small blood vessels. The earliest lesion of his condition forms through which process?
choices: Overgrowth of Cutibacterium acnes inside the sebaceous gland
Abnormal keratinization that plugs the opening of the hair follicle
Blockage of eccrine sweat ducts by keratin in the outer stratum corneum
Dilation of facial dermal blood vessels from neurovascular dysregulation
Invasion of the hair follicle wall by Staphylococcus aureus
questions.explanation: Open and closed **comedones** with inflammatory papules and pustules on oily facial skin in a teenager are **acne vulgaris**. Androgens enlarge sebaceous glands and raise sebum output, and **abnormal keratinization** of the follicle lining forms a plug (**microcomedo**), the first lesion. *Cutibacterium acnes* then grows in the trapped sebum and drives inflammation, so it explains the red papules and pustules but is a later step that does not create the plug.
questions.explanation_pt: **Comedões** abertos e fechados com pápulas e pústulas inflamatórias em pele facial oleosa de adolescente indicam **acne vulgar**. Os andrógenos aumentam as glândulas sebáceas e a produção de sebo, e a **queratinização anormal** do revestimento folicular forma um tampão (**microcomedão**), a primeira lesão. O *Cutibacterium acnes* então prolifera no sebo retido e promove inflamação, o que explica as pápulas e pústulas, mas é uma etapa posterior que não cria o tampão.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old woman has had itchy, raised, pink swellings on her trunk and arms for 4 days, starting after a cold. Each swelling has a pale center, lasts only a few hours and disappears without a mark, while new ones appear elsewhere. Firmly stroking her back produces a raised red line within minutes. She has no fever or joint pain. If one of the lesions were biopsied, which finding would be expected?
choices: Spongiosis with fluid between epidermal keratinocytes
Fibrinoid necrosis of small vessels with neutrophil nuclear dust
Band-like lymphocytes along the dermal-epidermal junction
Superficial dermal edema with a sparse perivascular infiltrate
Vacuolar interface change with scattered dead keratinocytes
questions.explanation: Itchy wheals that each fade within hours without a trace, with **dermatographism**, are **acute urticaria**. Mast cell **histamine** makes postcapillary venules leaky, so the biopsy shows **edema of the superficial dermis**, a **sparse perivascular infiltrate** (some eosinophils and neutrophils) and a **normal epidermis**. Fibrinoid necrosis with nuclear dust is **leukocytoclastic vasculitis**, seen in urticarial vasculitis, whose wheals last more than 24 hours, burn more than they itch and leave purpura or brown marks.
questions.explanation_pt: Urticas pruriginosas que somem em poucas horas sem deixar marca, com **dermografismo**, indicam **urticária aguda**. A **histamina** dos mastócitos aumenta a permeabilidade das vênulas pós-capilares, e a biópsia mostra **edema da derme superficial**, **infiltrado perivascular escasso** (alguns eosinófilos e neutrófilos) e **epiderme normal**. Necrose fibrinoide com poeira nuclear é **vasculite leucocitoclástica**, vista na vasculite urticariforme, cujas urticas duram mais de 24 horas, ardem mais do que coçam e deixam púrpura ou manchas acastanhadas residuais.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man has had a rash on his hands and forearms for 2 days. He feels well and has no fever. Exam shows many round, fixed lesions on the palms, backs of the hands and forearms. Each lesion has a dark red or blistered center, a pale middle ring and a red outer ring. There are two small erosions on the lower lip; the eyes and genitals are normal. Rubbing normal skin does not detach it. He had a similar rash last year. He takes no medications. Ten days ago he had a cluster of painful blisters on his upper lip. What is the most likely trigger of his rash?
choices: Herpes simplex virus infection
Hepatitis C virus infection
Group A streptococcal infection
A sulfonamide antibiotic
Parvovirus B19 infection
questions.explanation: Fixed **target lesions** with three zones on the hands and forearms, limited mucosal involvement, a well patient and **recurrences** are **erythema multiforme**. The most common trigger is **herpes simplex virus**, here a cold sore 10 days earlier; recurrent HSV explains the repeated episodes. Sulfonamides are classic triggers of **SJS/TEN**, which causes fever, widespread dusky macules with epidermal detachment and severe erosions of several mucosae, and he takes no drugs.
questions.explanation_pt: **Lesões em alvo** fixas com três zonas nas mãos e antebraços, acometimento mucoso limitado, bom estado geral e **recorrências** indicam **eritema multiforme**. O desencadeante mais comum é o **vírus herpes simples**, aqui um herpes labial 10 dias antes; o HSV recorrente explica os episódios repetidos. As sulfonamidas são desencadeantes clássicos da **SSJ/NET**, que causa febre, máculas violáceas extensas com descolamento epidérmico e erosões graves em várias mucosas, e ele não usa medicamentos.
